# relation

In [EhOsContract.Domain](domain-dsl.md), section `domain`.

```elixir
relation type
```

How two contexts relate: one of the eight context-mapping patterns.

**Arguments**

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Docs |
|------|------|----------|---------|------|
| <a id="domain-relation-type"></a>`type` | `:partnership \| :shared_kernel \| :separate_ways \| :customer_supplier \| :conformist \| :anticorruption_layer \| :open_host_service \| :published_language` | yes |  | The mapping pattern. |

**Options**

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Docs |
|------|------|----------|---------|------|
| <a id="domain-relation-upstream"></a>`upstream` | `atom` |  |  | The upstream context of a directed relation. |
| <a id="domain-relation-downstream"></a>`downstream` | `atom` |  |  | The downstream context of a directed relation. |
| <a id="domain-relation-between"></a>`between` | `list(atom)` |  | `[]` | The two contexts of a symmetric relation. |
| <a id="domain-relation-terms"></a>`terms` | `list({String.t, String.t})` |  | `[]` | Terms the relation translates, as pairs: the word of the first end, upstream or the first of `between:`, and the word of the second, each a term of its context's glossary. `{"Wizyta", "Wizyta"}`. |
| <a id="domain-relation-source"></a>`source` | `String.t` |  |  | Where the relation comes from in the material. |
